question: In a state, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Council of Ministers in a state is **collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly** as per Article 164 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This collective responsibility implies that the entire council works as a unit and stands or falls together in the assembly.
 
• If the State Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no-confidence against the council, all its members including the Chief Minister must resign.
 
• The Chief Minister serves as the leader of the Council of Ministers and communicates the collective decisions of the council to the Governor.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility ensures accountability of the executive (Council of Ministers) to the legislative body (State Assembly).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers on the CM’s advice. However, the council is not collectively responsible to the Governor.
 
• **Article 164**: This article lays down the provision of the council's collective responsibility to the legislative assembly and provides the constitutional framework for the functioning of the state government.
 
• **Vote of No-Confidence**: It is a parliamentary motion moved in the legislative assembly to demonstrate that the council no longer has the majority support of the house.
 
• **Individual vs. Collective Responsibility**: While individual ministers are responsible for their respective portfolios, collective responsibility ensures that the council acts unanimously and stands together on all decisions.
 
• **Constitutional Comparison**: This principle of collective responsibility is similar to the responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha at the central level.
